answer: Mutual Bluetooth co-location proof: each epoch the network pairs every agent with a random peer and both phones exchange a seed-stamped Bluetooth handshake, a beacon proving two bodies shared one room. Three auditors check the handshake logs and signal-strength curve, which no marble-smooth datacenter rack can fake. A farm of 1,000 identities in one hall forms one location cluster and is quarantined together, rewards frozen three epochs; spreading 1,000 phones across cities costs about $150,000 plus travel. One honest agent taps one handshake in seconds, free - its nectar of real presence.
